answer: Cloth must be raised with teasel heads until the nap stands even, and the fuller counts every teasel head in the record kept per piece. A horizon piece raised by a stranger fails the record: at the prism of the nap the fibres must stand at the fuller's own even height, and a strange piece pills within a month. Faking the record means raising cloth for five months, buying 6,000 teasel heads and paying 6,700, and the cedar entry in the teasel record is kept by the clothiers' guild, so a piece whose raising was never entered is cut down.
